text: The discount requires both Auto Pay and paper-free billing. Auto Pay can charge a bank account, debit card or credit card, but only a bank account or a Verizon Visa Card qualifies for the discount. Debit card enrollments made before February 14, 2024 keep the discount.

Up to $10 per line per month on myPlan Unlimited Ultimate, Unlimited Ultimate 1.0, Unlimited Plus and Unlimited Welcome. Up to $5 per line per month on older plans such as 5G Get More, 5G Do More, 5G Play More, 5G Start, Welcome Unlimited and One Unlimited for iPhone. 5G Home and LTE Home internet lines get $10 per line per month.
The discount starts with the next bill cycle after enrolling.

The discount amount depends on the plan, so changing plans can change it. Paying a bill once with a credit card online or in the My Verizon app removes the discount for that bill, and it shows up as a charge on the next bill.

Customers can call Verizon to dispute a charge on their bill. To keep the right to arbitration or small claims court, the dispute must also be sent in writing to the customer service address on the bill, or through the online Notice of Dispute form.

section: Paying while a dispute is open
text: Postpay customers must keep paying all charges, including disputed ones, until the dispute is resolved, unless the law says otherwise. Exception: charges related to a lost or stolen device do not have to be paid while they are being investigated.
Late fees are disputed separately, on the Bill Details page in My Verizon. See the Fees and Payments document for who is eligible for a late-fee credit.
If payment is not received by the due date, a late fee is charged where state law allows. The fee is the greater of two amounts: up to 5% of the unpaid balance per month, or a flat $10 per month.

A late fee can be disputed on the Bill Details page in My Verizon. It cannot be removed if the requester is not the Account Owner or Account Manager, has been a customer for less than 2 years, was billed more than 30 days ago, or already received a late-fee credit in the last 6 months.

The due date is on the first page of the bill. Account Owners and Account Managers can change it, except during bill processing (the 4 days after a billing period ends). Customers not on Auto Pay get an email or text reminder 2 days before the due date.

Paying in My Verizon, in a store, or by dialing #PMT is free. Paying through Customer Service costs a $10 Agent Assistance fee. Paying cash through third-party locations (CheckFreePay, Western Union) may cost up to $3.
A returned check costs $20 in CO, CT, ID, IN, NY and UT; $25 in AZ, CA, FL, IL, LA, MI, MO, NH, NV, OK, RI and WV; and $30 in all other states.
If an account is sent to collections, a collection fee may apply, capped at the legal maximum and never more than 18%.

doc: Billing Cycle, First Bill and Plan Changes (Verizon mobile)
text: The billing cycle starts on the day service is activated and repeats on the same dates every month. For example, service activated on November 19 has a billing period of November 19 to December 18.

doc: Billing Cycle, First Bill and Plan Changes (Verizon mobile)
text: The monthly plan charge for the upcoming period appears on the current bill. Usage-based charges, such as international usage, are billed after they happen.

doc: Billing Cycle, First Bill and Plan Changes (Verizon mobile)
section: Why the first bill is higher
text: A new customer's first bill includes the partial first billing period plus the next full month in advance. It may also include a one-time activation fee for each device added.

doc: Billing Cycle, First Bill and Plan Changes (Verizon mobile)
text: A line added in the middle of a cycle is charged a prorated amount for the remaining days of the current cycle, plus the full monthly charge for the next cycle.

doc: Billing Cycle, First Bill and Plan Changes (Verizon mobile)
text: When a plan changes mid-cycle, the bill shows prorated charges for both plans: the old plan up to the change date and the new plan from the change date to the end of the cycle.

doc: Billing Cycle, First Bill and Plan Changes (Verizon mobile)
text: One-time charges include activation fees, upgrade fees, device installment payments and accessories. Taxes, fees and surcharges also apply to them. Some charges are not final by the bill date and can appear on a later bill.

Government taxes and fees are set by federal, state and local governments; Verizon only bills and collects them. Surcharges are Verizon's own charges, not taxes or government-imposed fees. Both can vary by the state and locality of the service address, and both can change over time.
Helps cover government charges Verizon pays, such as number administration and license fees. From November 1, 2026 it rises from $0.21 to $0.26 per line per month for voice-capable devices.

section: Federal and State Universal Service Charges
text: Recover charges the government places on Verizon to support universal service programs.

Recovers regulatory and industry program costs (such as E911 and number portability), property taxes and network costs. It is charged per line and Verizon keeps it; it is not a tax. It was previously called the Administrative Charge and was renamed on June 3, 2022. Verizon reviews and adjusts it periodically.
